hook.text: Pollen is harmless. But if you have hay fever, your immune system treats it like a deadly invader.

buildup.text: Allergies occur when the immune system overreacts to harmless substances called allergens.

discovery.text: IgE antibodies bind to allergens and trigger mast cells to release histamine—causing sneezing and swelling.

twist.text: Allergies have increased dramatically in developed nations. The hygiene hypothesis suggests too-clean environments.

climax.text: Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that can cause blood pressure to drop fatally within minutes.

punchline.text: Your immune system is too good at its job. That's the problem.

quiz.question: What chemical causes allergy symptoms like sneezing and swelling?

details.summary: Allergies occur when the immune system mounts an exaggerated response to harmless substances like pollen, pet dander, or peanuts. Mast cells release histamine and other chemicals, causing symptoms from sneezing and hives to life-threatening anaphylaxis.
details.whyItMatters: Allergies affect over 50 million Americans annually and are increasing worldwide. Understanding the immune mechanisms behind allergies guides treatments from antihistamines to desensitization therapy and helps prevent severe reactions.
takeaways: Allergies are immune overreactions to harmless environmental substances
Mast cells release histamine, causing inflammation, swelling, and itching
Anaphylaxis is a severe whole-body allergic reaction requiring epinephrine

faq.question: Why do some people develop allergies while others do not?
faq.answer: Genetic predisposition plays a major role, but environmental factors like reduced childhood microbial exposure, diet, and pollution also matter. The hygiene hypothesis suggests overly clean environments leave the immune system with nothing to fight, so it overreacts to harmless substances.

faq.question: How does allergy desensitization therapy work?
faq.answer: Immunotherapy exposes the patient to gradually increasing doses of the allergen over months to years. This trains the immune system to produce blocking antibodies and regulatory T cells that suppress the allergic response, reducing sensitivity over time.
